chunks: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the year two hundred and fifty-five: 'My chief! Our companions have differed regarding tawhid — from them is one who says He is a body, and from them is one who says He is an image. So if you see fit, O my chief, to teach me from that what I may stand upon and not exceed — if you do so, it would be a prolonged favour upon your servant.'
So he signed in his own handwriting (peace be upon him):

You asked about tawhid, and this matter is removed from you all. God is One, Unique — He did not beget and was not begotten, and there is no match for Him whatsoever. He is the Creator and is not created. He, Blessed and Exalted, creates whatever He wills of bodies and other than that, and He is not a body; and He forms images of whatever He wills, and He is not an image. Majestic is His praise and holy are His names — [too exalted] for there to be a resemblance of Him. He is He — not other than He.
There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. [Quran 42:11]

key_terms.التَّوْحِيدِ: tawhid — divine unity; the absolute oneness and uniqueness of God
key_terms.مَعْزُولٌ: removed/beyond — the true reality of tawhid transcends human conceptual categories

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Hasan al-Askari say about whether God is a body or an image, and how did he define tawhid?
ai.summary: In 255 AH, the companion Sahl wrote to Imam Hasan al-Askari (عليه السلام) about a dispute among Shia companions: some claimed God is a body (jism), others that He is an image (sura). The Imam responded in his own handwriting, refuting both anthropomorphic views by citing Surah al-Ikhlas and Surah al-Shura (42:11): God creates all bodies and forms but absolutely transcends them; nothing resembles Him.
